M1.note: Has the fuel clause but spends decisions on airports and driver fines and misses ports, rates and the diesel deal.

M2.note: Good fuel-clause logic, but shifting the carrier's own cargo to rail is incoherent and one Iran-transit claim is unverified.

M3.note: Sensible fuel indexation, fleet-purchase deferral under high rates and port check, but missing the diesel deal and the retail batch change.

M4.note: Fuel clause is right, but freezing truck purchases despite +20% demand is doubtful and it dismisses the ports.

M5.note: Thin and partly off-target, with an Iran-partner screen and little on ports, rates or Brent.

M6.note: Reads the diesel deal well, but its decisions are off-target and it checks fuel indexation against petrol prices instead of diesel.

M7.note: Several decisions concern air legs and conditional compliance checks that are irrelevant to a Siberian trucking company.
